dedupe_keys.name: nestli umar living lab hvac control benchmark

description: nestli publishes a reusable digital-twin benchmark for the UMAR living unit in Empa's NEST demonstrator at Dübendorf, Switzerland. The Empa repository describes a calibrated EnergyPlus model wrapped as a Functional Mock-up Unit through EnergyPlusToFMU. Calibration measurements were collected at one-minute intervals, and the model runs at the same temporal resolution. Users can override room temperature setpoints and change weather or building operation to compare building-automation controllers. The repository provides Python example code, YAML configuration and a Docker deployment option. Source is public and free under AGPL-3.0. EnergyPlus and Python are prerequisites. A limitation is that the model represents one living lab; the README does not establish calibration accuracy, the measurement date range or transferability to other buildings. The documented outcome is a calibrated co-simulation environment for controller benchmarking, not a verified energy-saving result. This case connects a real building demonstrator to the catalogue's EnergyPlus model (model-energyplus). No executable, measurement data or model archive was downloaded during this review.
name: nestli: UMAR living-lab HVAC-control benchmark
notes: G7 G7-0040. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-27; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability.  Cited as: Khayatian, Cai, Bojarski, Heer and Bollinger (2022). Benchmarking HVAC controller performance with a digital twin. CEN2022. https://www.enerarxiv.org/page/thesis.html?id=3819.
outcomes: Published calibrated one-minute EnergyPlus/FMUs and a co-simulation benchmark for HVAC controllers; no quantitative controller benefit established from the README.
